source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Seal and label the specimen correctly and use the facility-approved leak-resistant transport packaging","B":"Loosen the container cap so pressure changes during transit can escape through the specimen opening","C":"Remove patient identification because the pneumatic carrier itself provides adequate specimen identity","D":"Place an unsealed specimen directly in the carrier because tube systems prevent leakage by design"}}
source_row.rationale: Specimens must be properly identified and transported in secure, leak-resistant containers according to laboratory and facility policy. Pneumatic systems require validation for the specimen type; some high-risk specimens should not be sent by pneumatic tube.
source_row.source_detail: Specimen transport: leakproof primary container and sealable leakproof transport packaging; MMWR Suppl. 2012; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Guidelines for Safe Work Practices in Diagnostic Laboratories
source_row.stem: A facility permits a routine laboratory specimen to be sent through its validated pneumatic tube system. What should the nurse do before sending it?
